name: Calculator observed-UI baseline
goal: Exercise the observed Windows Calculator Standard-mode controls with explicit result assertions. Functional checks are provisional UI-derived expectations, not user-approved business requirements.

requirements.text: Provisional: Standard mode exposes a visible result display and Clear resets it to zero.
requirements.source: Observed Header, CalculatorResults and clearButton; acceptance expectation proposed from control semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: After Clear, result text is exactly Display is 0.

requirements.text: Provisional: basic arithmetic produces mathematically correct integer results.
requirements.source: Observed plusButton, minusButton, multiplyButton, divideButton and equalButton.

requirements.text: Provisional: Backspace removes the final entered digit.
Provisional: Square and Square root perform the named operations.
Provisional: memory store, recall and clear function as named.
Use observed selectors, executable cases and explicit assertions; keep healing off for the first run.
acceptanceCriteria: Suite uses observed UI Automation IDs and explicit assertions.

requirements.text: Close inspection session before execution, poll to completion and provide summary, detailed and requirement-coverage reports.
acceptanceCriteria: Inspection session is closed before test_run.
Finished job and report paths are recorded.

risks: No functional requirements or acceptance criteria were supplied; UI01–UI05 are provisional and do not establish business acceptance.
Attached desktop sessions share application state; every case explicitly clears the display and memory case cleans up its memory.
Only observed Standard mode is covered. Existing history may remain.
Desktop execution requires an interactive Windows session; locale-dependent text may affect exact assertions.
questions: Which Calculator product/version and modes are required? This run targets the observed Windows Calculator Standard mode.
Are proposed UI01–UI05 functional expectations approved, or are there source requirements to replace them?
What are required precision, rounding, overflow, divide-by-zero and negative-square-root behaviors?
Are decimals, percentages, keyboard input, history, converters, accessibility and persistence in scope?

scenarios.name: Standard mode and reset
preconditions: One Calculator window open in Standard mode
steps: Assert Standard mode header and visible result.

scenarios.name: Memory lifecycle
steps: Clear all memory and assert recall disabled.
scenarios.expected: Stored value recalled correctly and memory cleared.
